fix.note: The data were 'made available by district magistrate Vishak G' (HT, 7 January 2026). The percentages are right for all nine seats; the counts printed beside two of them are not. The pair 2,98,231 of 3,59,016 gives 16.93%, so it is Mohanlalganj's and was printed under Lucknow Cantonment as well. Lucknow Central's printed pair (2,22,598 of 3,72,000) gives 40.16%, not its 34.61%. Subtracting the eight other seats from the district totals gives Cantonment 3,65,590 before, and the two draft counts are swapped: Cantonment 3,65,590 to 2,22,598 is 39.11%, and Central 3,72,000 to 2,43,246 is 34.61%. That matches Dainik Bhaskar (Cantonment 3.65 lakh to 2.22 lakh, Central 3.72 lakh to 2.43 lakh). No CEO or DEO table by seat was found.

fix.claim: ThePrint reported in August 2026 that, on the final roll published in April 2026, Lucknow again had the largest fall in Uttar Pradesh from the roll before the revision, 9.14 lakh or 22.89 per cent, which the paper called deletions. It is a net fall: it counts names added after the draft as well as names removed.

evidence: The final electoral roll for Uttar Pradesh also saw the highest deletions in Lucknow, percentage-wise (22.89 per cent) as well as in absolute numbers—9.14 lakh.
why: Verbatim, ThePrint (Apoorva Mandhani), 28 August 2026. 9.14 lakh / 39.94 lakh = 22.9%, so the base is the roll before the revision and the figure is the net change to the final roll. The original claim called it 'the highest deletions' in the site's own voice; a net change must not be called names removed, so the fix attributes the word to the paper and says what it is.

fix.claim: The Times of India, in its own analysis of the revision's figures, put Lucknow Cantonment's fall at 34.18 per cent, over 1.24 lakh names, the highest rate in the state, and Lucknow Central's at 28.88 per cent, 1.07 lakh. Both are larger than the 2022 winning margins of 39,512 and 10,935. The paper does not say which roll its figures run to; they are lower than the draft's fall, so they appear to be the net fall to the final roll, which counts new voters too.

evidence: Ravidas Mehrotra’s Lucknow Central seat recorded a staggering 1.07 lakh deletions, accounting for 28.88% of the electorate, nearly 10 times his winning margin of 10,935 votes. Deputy chief minister Brajesh Pathak’s Lucknow Cantonment seat witnessed the highest deletion rate in the state at 34.18%, translating to over 1.24 lakh voters removed from rolls, far exceeding his victory margin of 39,512.
why: Verbatim, Times of India (Arvind Chauhan), 18 April 2026. The story says 'A detailed analysis of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2026 voter data' and never says 'after the final roll', so that phrase in the first claim is the first reader's inference. 34.18% of the implied 3,65,590 is 1,24,959, below the draft's 39.11%, consistent with a net fall to the final roll. Margins match data/uttarpradesh/raw/results_2022.csv. The source of the paper's seat figures is not stated; if it was compiled from the named lists it would fall under the case rules, and nothing in the story says either way.
